translations.answer: Maintainer's note: The WORLD Jacobian's twist is expressed in world coordinates, with linear velocity corresponding to the point attached to the target joint; LOCAL is expressed in joint local coordinates and corresponds to the joint center. The connection is given by J_world = action(data.oMi[k]) * J_local. To obtain joint local velocity, first call forwardKinematics(model, data, q, qdot), then read data.v[id]. If only the same actuator point's velocity is to be expressed in world coordinates, separately rotate the linear and angular components using data.oMi[id].rotation(), and do not introduce an extra translation. Jcom is the world coordinate expression of the system's center of mass velocity, and does not follow the world origin action point explanation of the WORLD spatial twist.
translations.applicability: Applicable to the Joint Jacobian, data.v, and Jcom conventions in this period of Pinocchio; Frame API and LOCAL_WORLD_ALIGNED must be verified against corresponding version documentation separately.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is lacking.
translations.details.attempts.0: Maintainer provides data.oMi[1].rotation.T * Jc comparison; author applies rotation and reports significant error reduction.
translations.details.attempts.1: Author compares fixed base and FreeFlyer, setting both base poses to unit; matrix error reduces to ~1e-8 to 1e-10 at unit pose.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: First determine the coordinate system and actuator point of the Jacobian being compared; rotate Pinocchio Jcom to the target local coordinate system and compare.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Compare CRBA with unit base rotation and non-unit rotation; confirm difference is only due to floating base representation.
translations.details.diagnostics.2: Cross-validate quality matrix using RNEA and appropriate reference frame, rather than comparing element-wise between two libraries.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Compare Jcom before converting both sides to the same coordinate expression; original thread used data.oMi[1].rotation.T * Pinocchio Jc.
translations.details.effective_fixes.1: Read joint local velocity by first calling forwardKinematics(model, data, q, qdot), then use data.v[id]; only change coordinate expression by rotating linear/angular components, not translating the actuator point.
translations.details.environments.0: 2018 Pinocchio Python/C++; MuJoCo comparison; user provides minimal URDF, two-legged URDF state, and full matrix output; specific release version not mentioned.
translations.details.limits.0: Original thread did not provide a general MuJoCo↔Pinocchio quality matrix base transformation formula, and did not fully close all bias term differences.
translations.details.limits.1: data.oMi[1] is only suitable for the minimal model's first target joint; actual system must use correct joint ID.
translations.details.outcomes.0: Author confirms Jcom rotation difference is significantly reduced and WORLD/LOCAL explanation is clear.
translations.details.outcomes.1: Author obtains nearly identical quality matrices on both sides at unit base rotation, and attributes remaining non-unit rotation difference to floating base representation.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why are the first three columns of the floating base Jcom not the identity matrix, and are the Pinocchio and MuJoCo Jcom/matrix values different?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: What actuator point and coordinate system does Pinocchio's WORLD, LOCAL Jacobian, and data.v[id] correspond to?
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Pinocchio Jcom is expressed in world coordinates; user's MuJoCo comparison is using the waist local coordinate system.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: Pinocchio's floating base velocity, acceleration, and force components are expressed in first body coordinates, while MuJoCo's comparison matrix is expressed in world coordinates.
translations.details.symptoms.0: At non-unit base pose, Pinocchio Jcom has a ~1e-2 off-diagonal term in the translation block, while user expects an identity matrix.
translations.details.symptoms.1: Fixed base quality matrix is consistent on both sides, but becomes significantly different after adding FreeFlyer and rotating the base non-unit.

translations.source.title: Pinocchio and MuJoCo Floating Base Jcom and Inertial Matrix Differences Need to Be Aligned by Reference Frame Representation
translations.title: What Actuator Point and Coordinate System Does Pinocchio's WORLD and LOCAL Jacobian Correspond To? How Does data.v[id] Only Change the Coordinate Expression?
